angle: product strategist — whitespace, structural moats, positioning, and what "#1" can credibly mean
definition:
"Best Mac cleaner in the world" must be narrowed or it is simply false, and the author should stop trying to defend it.

The surface-area gap is not closable solo in 12 months. CleanMyMac 5 ships malware scanning, an uninstaller, duplicate and photo dedup, a menu-bar monitor, 13 localizations, Setapp distribution and a 10-year brand behind 29M claimed downloads. Mole — verified on mole.fit today — sells a five-tool native GUI at $19 one-time for two Macs with lifetime updates, in ten languages, with 47K+ GitHub stars on its free CLI acting as top-of-funnel and a FAQ entry literally titled "How does Mole compare to CleanMyMac?". DaisyDisk has an 18-year-refined visualization and an App Store Editors' Choice. A solo developer will not out-feature any of them.

What IS winnable, outright, inside 12 months, and verifiable by a stranger in under two minutes:

1. **#1 on safety.** The only Mac cleaner with exactly one destructive call, and that call is reversible. Mole trashes only in `analyze`; its `clean` does not. PureMac's own README concedes that dashboard/category cleanup, scheduled auto-clean, Trash emptying and Docker/Xcode runtime cleanup delete permanently, and that it escalates to root via NSAppleScript with an admitted TOCTOU race. DevCleaner calls `removeItem` directly. mac-cleanup-py is `sudo rm -rf`. CleanMyMac auto-selects irreversible Document Versions and Downloads. Nobody ships the absolute version of this promise.

2. **#1 on honesty.** The only Mac cleaner that reports a measured `statfs` free-space delta rather than the sum of the bytes it moved. This is currently a category of one — not "better than competitors," but a thing zero competitors do.

3. **Best-in-class on versioned developer toolchains.** The only cleaner that knows you have four NDKs and build with one, that five of six Gradle distributions are referenced by nothing, that 6.0 of 8.2 GB of DerivedData belongs to a project you built yesterday, and that all three of your simulator runtimes were used yesterday so the correct offer is zero.

The claim to make: **"#1 on safety and truthfulness. Best-in-class on developer toolchains. Not the biggest."** The niche — iOS/Android/JVM developers on Apple Silicon who have been burned by a cleaner or refuse to install one — is narrow, but it is real, it pays, and it is loud on HN, Reddit and Homebrew. Homebrew analytics prove the audience preference: Pearcleaner 43,790 installs/year vs CleanMyMac 4,738, a 9.2:1 ratio for a free, open, undo-capable tool over the market leader.

angle: Principal engineer — architecture to hold 100+ catalogue rules across multiple reclaim mechanisms without losing the one-destructive-primitive property; read FileSafety.swift, Scanner.swift, Models.swift, WorkspaceContracts.swift, LocalCleaningRepository.swift, AGENTS.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, and verified `xcrun simctl help runtime` output on this machine.
definition: Not "best Mac cleaner" for consumers — that requires an uninstaller, duplicates, photo dedupe, malware, localization, 13 languages and a support org, and CleanMyMac owns it. The winnable #1 is: **the developer Mac cleaner whose numbers are provably true.** Three claims nobody else can make simultaneously, because each of their architectures forecloses one: (1) every byte is measured against a real statfs delta and the word "freed" is bound to that one number — Mole, PureMac and CleanMyMac all report summed file sizes; (2) every offered item carries machine-checkable evidence for *why* it is dead (orphan WorkspacePath, simctl lastUsedAt, "no gradle-wrapper.properties references 5.4.1", CACHEDIR.TAG) rather than "it is big and it is called cache"; (3) the reclaim path is Trash-or-the-vendor's-own-verb, never `rm`, never root — PureMac's category cleanup is a permanent delete with NSAppleScript root escalation and a self-admitted TOCTOU race, so it structurally cannot copy this. Add a published, cited, fixture-backed rule catalogue and the product is auditable in a way a closed subscription binary can never be.

angle: Trust and safety architect — how ViggoClean keeps checkable safety as its moat while coverage and permissions expand 10x
definition: Not "most GB." Every competitor already CLAIMS safety — MacPaw's CLI wiki says "Nothing is deleted until you confirm" (then ships `--force`), PureMac's README says "review the results before removal" (then permanently deletes on its main path and escalates via NSAppleScript), and Mole publishes a genuinely serious SECURITY_AUDIT.md (fetched today, updated 2026-09-13) describing guarded bash helpers. All of it is prose. Not one of them gives a stranger an artifact they can RUN to check the claim. #1 from this angle means exactly three things: (1) ViggoClean is the only Mac cleaner whose safety properties are a numbered, published invariant list where each invariant maps to a named test and an exact source line, and whose refusal behaviour a skeptic can reproduce on their own Mac in under five minutes with one command; (2) it is the only one that reports freed space by MEASUREMENT (statfs f_bavail delta) rather than by assertion, including the screen where it says "0 bytes freed — these files are in the Trash"; (3) it is the only one that publishes what it REFUSES to do and why, and can prove the refusal. That is a category of one, it is defensible against a funded incumbent because incumbents cannot copy it without giving up their coverage, and it is large enough — every developer who has been burned by a cleaner — to be a real business. What it is NOT: #1 on breadth. Against MacPaw's headcount and Mole's 67.7k-star velocity, a solo author does not win "most categories," and chasing that is how the safety position gets spent.
